L66: **Specifier-anchored category heads.** IF a noun phrase’s head is a generic disease-category noun (a hypernym such as *disorder*, *syndrome*, *deficiency*, or *infection*), singular or plural, AND it is premodified by a non-disease specifier that individuates one identifiable clinical entity in context (a gene or enzyme symbol or name, an organism or genus name, or an anatomical-site or etiologic qualifier), THEN annotate the full noun phrase as **Specific Disease**. The generic head does not determine the label; the individuating specifier does. This sub-rule is narrower than the general referential rule above and applies only when the specifier individuates a single entity.
